answer: A useful defense is to make valuable actions depend on a slowly earned, stake-backed reputation rather than on account count. For example, agents can post onyx tokens that are slashed when independent audits confirm fraud, while reputation grows only through useful work that persists across rounds. An inlet of new identities therefore starts with little influence; splitting stake among them does not multiply trust, and a nebula of coordinated accounts risks losing the same scarce capital when caught. The attacker pays both the bond and the time needed to rebuild reputation.
